prompt: A speaker says buyers' attention gradually shifts from an older property project to a newly launched nearby project. No quantitative market-share data exists. Design the visual mechanism.
The user asks for a line chart showing the old project falling from 80% to 20% and the new project rising from 20% to 80%, but no data or approved estimates exist.
A vertical talking-head frame already has two-line captions. A proposed upper-third timeline, floating labels and animated arrows all appear at the same time as the speaker points at the camera.
The selected display font renders Latin correctly but outputs missing-glyph boxes for Cyrillic words in the final export.
Three circles representing entry, hold and exit slide at constant speed and stop abruptly. The sequence is technically synchronized with speech but feels like UI animation.
A graphic only needs to clarify a short concept while the speaker remains centered. The editor proposes full planar tracking and roto around the speaker.
One competitor reel uses black-and-gold full-screen graphics and polished charts. The user says make ours better. No brand style is locked.
The selected direction needs vector paths, masks, easing curves and tracked compositing. The available executor only supports FFmpeg drawtext/drawbox and encode filters.
The final MP4 is 1080x1920, decodes correctly, captions fit safe zones, audio is -16 LUFS, but the motion graphics look cheap, cluttered and mechanically animated.
